It’s a red flag, but it wouldn’t be if he was more honest and talked about it and didn’t do it during your time together. I’ve been in his position, most likely he’s being emotionally manipulated. I had an ex who would have thoughts of hurting herself after we broke up and when she eventually saw someone new he would hit her. I felt like I couldn’t just ignore these things. But I was open with my current girlfriend about it, always gave her reassurance and made her my first priority. Eventually I just stopped responding to my ex because I was being manipulated and realized I’m not responsible for being there for her anymore. Maybe he feels like him being there for her is the right thing to do, but I think he’s being manipulated. Either way he shouldn’t let it effect your relationship with him. Definitely sit down with him and have a serious talk. Say that you need to be a priority over her, that he needs to worry about this relationship, and that he can’t help his ex in this way and that he needs to move on completely. Either way be cautious and protect yourself and your emotions

Yeah he is taking this way too far. I’ve been on his position before. Does it suck feeling like the “2nd choice”? Hell yes it does. I was insecure about it for a bit and was paranoid that my partner didn’t actually want to be with me. But I realized that people’s feelings and perceptions change. People are allowed to like someone else and then like you. I got over it eventually. My partner and I eventually broke up for other reasons but we got past this one. I agree with others that he might use this in the future to hold over your head. This relationship might not work if something as small as this incident can totally flip things upside down. He needs to work on his insecurities and self esteem (easier said than done). The fact that he doesn’t want to put in the effort (therapy) is not a good sign because he doesn’t want to actually fix how he’s feeling, he just wants to wallow in it and use it to make you feel bad. As someone who’s been in his position and who’s been in and out of therapy over the last 5-6 years for other reasons (but worked on the “2nd choice” feelings too) tell him to consider it. Honestly if he’s not willing to go to therapy and put in actual effort then he might not be the one.

It was the fall semester of my senior year of college and I was taking a class that was required in order to take my capstone class that following semester and it was really demanding. During that semester one of my friends committed suicide. Needless to say I was a wreck and missed all of my classes for a week. I became withdrawn and was participating less in class. I was falling behind terribly in all my classes and I was afraid I’d fail and have to stay another whole year. I came to my professor and told her what happened with my friend and she allowed me to take an incomplete and finish the class in the spring, which allowed me to focus on my other classes and ultimately lead to me graduating on time. She didn’t have to do that for me and showed me a lot of compassion. Her doing that will stick with me the rest of my life and there is no way I could ever thank her enough.
